about: The managed runner states the three clients are proved against (docs/managed-runner-design.md,
"Server and three client interfaces"): one file, read by the apiserver, @orbit/shared, the web and
OrbitKit (macOS and iOS).
`capabilities`: `GET /api/auth/capabilities` answers. `offered` is whether a client shows any
managed UI (`managedRunnersOffered`). The apiserver spec checks the two switch answers against its
own route; the others are what an older or newer server could send.
`states`: each case's `server` is what the apiserver stores and knows (`enabled` is the switch,
`available` whether its environment profile is valid, `eligible` the eligibility answer for an owner
without a mapping, `ownerDisabled` whether an administrator disabled the account; `mapping` lists the managed_runner fields that differ from a blank row, with
`lastErrorCode` naming the manager's stored reason and `capacityShort` a capacity refusal; `runner`
is the runner row's heartbeat), all at `now` with `heartbeatFreshMs`. `status` is the body
`GET /api/managed-runner` answers for it, public ids and their twins included: the apiserver spec
derives it from `server` with managedRunnerStatus and the public id mapping, and fails if it differs.
`display` is what every client shows for that status (`managedRunnerDisplay`, null: no managed UI).
`title` and `detail` are the exact words; `detail` is the server's reason sentence when the status
carries one. `retry` offers Retry (POST /managed-runner/retry with the read revision), `ensure` offers
Set up (POST /managed-runner/ensure), `signIn` points at the runner's runtimes in Infrastructure.
`acceptsWork`: a message or turn sent now is accepted and waits for the runner, so a client does not
refuse it as offline. `startsNewSession`: a first session in the managed default workspace can start
(the runner was found ready with `initialProvider`); before that no client offers a default engine
there. `moving`: read the status again soon (MANAGED_RUNNER_STATUS_POLL_SECONDS).
A reason `code` is an open string: a server can add one (C6b adds ACCOUNT_DISABLED), so a client
shows any reason's `message` and never needs to know its code. The two `failed`/`preparing` cases
with REASON_FROM_A_NEWER_SERVER hold that, and so does ACCOUNT_DISABLED ("asleep, its account
disabled"): the server offers no action and no wake, so nothing is accepted for it.
`newer`: answers this server cannot give but a newer one could, made from the `available` case
with `patch` applied: a management state or a contract version this client does not know. Each
must decode and show no managed UI (`display` null), never fail or wait.
`copy` is MANAGED_RUNNER_COPY's action words, the same in every client.
